summary: Build practical community health and nutrition skills. Learn MUAC screening, IYCF protocols, and mHealth data collection to improve local public health outcomes
lede: Community health and nutrition training covers how to assess nutritional needs and plan community-level interventions. It is intended for community health workers and public health field staff, with practice in MUAC screening, dietary diversity assessment, infant and young child feeding counseling, and integrating hygiene promotion into nutrition work.
audienceIntro: This course is specifically designed for frontline public health staff and community development professionals responsible for implementing and monitoring grassroots health initiatives.
modules: Foundations of Community Health and Nutrition
Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Feeding (IYCF)
Behavior Change Communication (BCC) in Public Health
Mobile Health (mHealth) and Field Data Collection
prerequisites: This foundational course is designed for frontline practitioners. Participants should have basic familiarity with community outreach or local health systems. No advanced medical training or prior coding experience is required. Familiarity with operating a smartphone or tablet is recommended for the mobile data collection modules.
